amendments.body: Add invariant enforcement for `denitrifier_activity_index` in `invariants.rs:enforce_invariants`. All other 0–1 indices (`biofilter_maturity_index`, `maturity_index`, `nuisance_index`, etc.) are clamped in `enforce_invariants` (lines 21–49), but `denitrifier_activity_index` is not. A corrupted save or deserialization of an out-of-range value (e.g., > 1.0) would propagate unchecked into the denitrification rate calculation at `nitrogen_cycle.rs:537`, amplifying the denitrification rate beyond the intended ceiling.
amendments.rationale: Defense against corrupt saves or deserialization drift. Every other bounded index in MicrobeState is clamped in enforce_invariants; this is an omission that breaks the pattern and could produce nonsensical denitrification rates from loaded state.

amendments.body: Add `check_non_negative` invariant validation for `cumulative_n2_export_mg_n` in `invariants.rs:validate_invariants_inner`. This field is a monotonically increasing cumulative counter (only incremented at `nitrogen_cycle.rs:570`) and is part of the nitrogen budget array (`budget.rs`). A negative value from a corrupted save would silently unbalance the nitrogen budget without any diagnostic error.
amendments.rationale: Consistency with how all other nitrogen-bearing totals are validated (e.g., nitrate_mg_n_total at line 83, nitrite_mg_n_total at line 82). A negative cumulative export would produce a phantom nitrogen surplus in the budget.

amendments.body: Add `check_non_negative` invariant validation for the five new denitrification process params (`denitrification_vmax_mg_n_per_l_per_hour`, `denitrification_k_no3_mg_n_per_l`, `denitrification_k_doc_mg_c_per_l`, `denitrification_pore_water_mixing_factor`, `denitrification_activity_maturation_days`) in the process params validation block at `invariants.rs:220–288`. The code applies `.max(0.01)` and `safe_rate()` defensively at the call site (`nitrogen_cycle.rs:531–538`), but all other kinetic process params (aob_vmax, nob_vmax, decomposer_vmax, etc.) are validated up front in invariants. Missing this creates an inconsistency where invalid configs are silently clamped rather than rejected.
amendments.rationale: Other kinetic params are validated in the invariant block (lines 230–240). The new denitrification params follow the same pattern but lack validation, so a negative vmax or negative maturation_days would be silently clamped to 0 or 1 respectively without any user-visible diagnostic.

amendments.body: Update the stale doc comment on `DENITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N` in `process.rs:25–27` which still reads 'Reserved for E4b (denitrification implementation). When wiring, add...' — denitrification is now implemented and this constant is actively used at `nitrogen_cycle.rs:572`. The comment should reflect current usage rather than future intent.
amendments.rationale: Misleading documentation. A developer reading this constant would believe denitrification is not yet wired, when it is. Minor but worth cleaning up as part of this change since the constant was exercised for the first time here.

payload.summary: The chloride protection and denitrification implementation is mechanistically correct: stoichiometry checks out (DOC:N ratio ≈ 1.071, alkalinity production 1/14.007 meq/mg N), mass balance is maintained across N and C budgets, and the nitrogen budget array correctly accounts for N₂ export as a permanent loss term. The chloride-nitrite hazard formula matches the spec and the integration test is well-structured with salt-treatment vs. matched-control vs. protection-disabled arms. The one test failure (thermal_reproduction_penalty) is pre-existing and unrelated to these changes. Four amendments are proposed, all relating to missing invariant/validation coverage for the new denitrification state fields and process parameters — patterns that are consistently applied to all existing analogous fields but were omitted for the new ones.
